program_narrative: Program DB2STAT is a called (subprogram) DB2 statistics collector. The caller passes LS-STAT-REQUEST, whose 4-character function code selects one action per call: INIT records the start timestamp, declares the session temporary table SESSION.DBSTATS (tolerating SQLCODE -601 if it already exists) and inserts a zero statistics row for the caller's program ID; UPDT copies the caller's rows-read, inserted, updated, deleted, commit and rollback counts into that row; TERM records the end timestamp, computes elapsed time and an estimated CPU time (65 percent of elapsed), writes them to the row and displays the statistics; DISP reads the row back and displays it. After every SQL statement the program checks SQLCODE: on success it sets return code 0; on failure it sets ERR-TEXT, return code 12 and calls the common error routine ERRPROC. An unknown function code also sets return code 12 and calls ERRPROC. Control returns to the caller with GOBACK.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Main dispatcher: route the caller's request by function code (LS-FUNCTION)
IF function code is 'INIT' THEN  -- FUNC-INIT
ELSE IF function code is 'UPDT' THEN  -- FUNC-UPDT
ELSE IF function code is 'TERM' THEN  -- FUNC-TERM
ELSE IF function code is 'DISP' THEN  -- FUNC-DISP
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Main dispatcher: route the caller's request by function code (LS-FUNCTION)
IF function code is 'INIT' THEN  -- FUNC-INIT
  CALL 1000-initialize
ELSE IF function code is 'UPDT' THEN  -- FUNC-UPDT
  CALL 2000-update-stats
ELSE IF function code is 'TERM' THEN  -- FUNC-TERM
  CALL 3000-terminate
ELSE IF function code is 'DISP' THEN  -- FUNC-DISP
  CALL 4000-display-stats
ELSE
  SET err_text = 'Invalid function code'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

annotations.note: EVALUATE TRUE over 88-level names of LS-FUNCTION: first matching WHEN wins, so it is translated as an IF / ELSE IF chain
ERR-TEXT belongs to ERR-MESSAGE in copybook ERRHAND, which is passed to ERRPROC by 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE

paragraphs.name: 3100-CALC-TIMES
pseudocode: -- Derive elapsed time and an estimated CPU time
COMPUTE ws_elapsed_time = NUMVAL(first 15 chars of ws_end_time) - NUMVAL(first 15 chars of ws_start_timestamp)  -- !! REVIEW: ambiguous, see annotation
COMPUTE ws_cpu_time = ws_cpu_time * 0.65  -- MULTIPLY 0.65 BY: CPU time is estimated as 65% of elapsed time, not measured

-- Derive elapsed time and an estimated CPU time

SET ws_cpu_time = ws_elapsed_time
COMPUTE ws_cpu_time = ws_cpu_time * 0.65  -- MULTIPLY 0.65 BY: CPU time is estimated as 65% of elapsed time, not measured

annotations.note: The second NUMVAL has no FUNCTION keyword; without a REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC clause it is not an intrinsic-function reference. Also, the first 15 characters of a TIME STAMP value are a date-time string; NUMVAL of it does not yield seconds. The intended unit of the result is not determinable from the source

paragraphs.name: 4000-DISPLAY-STATS

SQL SELECT rows_read, rows_inserted, rows_updated, rows_deleted, commits, rollbacks, cpu_time, elapsed_time
